messages:
maria: Quick postmortem follow-up. We agreed to stop treating every spike as a page and instead create a short priority taxonomy + per-alert guidance. Draft below 12 please ack and add owners/ETAs.

Draft taxonomy & follow-ups:
- priority=A (page immediately): SEV1 / customer-visible data loss, crash, or security. (owner: ryan)
- priority=B (page for sustained signal >3m): infra capacity/backbone regressions. (owner: sam)
- priority=C (no page, ticket only): noisy transient alerts, short-lived network blips. (owner: maria)
- dedupe strategy: fingerprint+ttl per alert-class, emit "suppressed_by_dedupe" metric. (owner: sam)
- thresholds: run p95/p99 sweep and choose cutoffs with baseline FP estimate. (owner: jess)
- rollout policy: canary 2%->10%->100% with auto-rollback if error-rate delta >5% in 30m. (owner: jess)
- recurring patterns: run 90d incident clustering and return top noisy alert classes. (owner: priya)

sam: Ack for dedupe and priority mapping for infra cases. ETA: PR with matcher templates + tests by Fri. I'll include example TTLs: cache-errors=180s, network-blips=45s. Will also add a telemetry flag so suppressed events still increment counters.

jess: Ack for thresholds + rollout. ETA: baseline job + CSV by Wed, PR with canary plan Thu. Need last 14d p95/p99 for model-inference; @priya can you post?

priya: From dashboards: model-inference p95=160ms p99=420ms (14d). Incident export link for clustering: https://redwood/incidents/export?days=90

maria: Good. Ryan, can you take the Priority=A examples and write a short rule doc so oncall knows what escalates to product/exec? Maybe 2-3 bullet examples per priority. ETA Tue EOD.

ryan: Will do. Proposal: Priority=A includes data-loss, tenant-facing auth failures, production DB write path failures. Priority=B includes service degradation affecting >10% traffic or sustained p95 regressions. Draft by Tue.

alerts-bot: Reminder: created ticket https://github.com/redwood/ops/issues/1102 "alert-priority-taxonomy" and scheduled recurring review meeting weekly Thursdays 11:00 UTC.

sam: On dedupe semantics: I recommend aggregation (send a single summary page per window) for B/C classes and full page for A. Also emit event_count and distinct_hosts metrics.

jess: For thresholds, I'll simulate alert volume at candidate cutoffs and compute false-positive rate. Plan: pick cutoff at the knee where pages drop 60% but true positives remain >95% (based on historical incidents).

priya: For recurring detection, I'll cluster by alert name + deploy-tag + service and surface the top-12 noisy signals. Will add a column whether deploy correlation exists. ETA: Thu.

maria: Great. Owner/ETA recap: ryan (priority doc Tue), sam (dedupe PR Fri), jess (baseline Wed, PR Thu), priya (incident clustering Thu). Weekly review Thursday. If anyone needs to change owner or ETA, tag here.

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/alerts/pull/499 - includes fingerprint matcher + "suppressed_by_dedupe" metric. r? @maria @jess

jess: Reviewing. One note: make dedupe TTL configurable per alert via metadata so we can tweak without code changes.

maria: Agreed. We'll require a feature-flagged rollout for dedupe changes and add rollback criteria: automatic revert if pages_sent increases by >10% or error-rate worsens by >5% within 1h.

ryan: Added priority examples to the RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood/ops/pull/217 - please review and comment.

priya: Incident clustering finished: top noisy alerts -> redis-error, dns-flap, model-inference-spike. Deploy correlation for redis-error is high (70%). Posting CSV to the ticket.

maria: Thanks team. I'll update the follow-up tracker with GH links and mark this thread closed once all PRs are merged. Final ask: please add a one-line PR description that references the ticket so we can audit changes later. :thumbsup:
